title: 2.3 Granite Rapids-D: Intel Xeon 6 SoC for vRAN, Edge, Networking, and Storage
problem: vRAN (virtualized radio access networks), edge servers, networking, and storage workloads have diverging requirements: compute-optimized SKUs need scalar/data-parallel performance with low-latency high-bandwidth memory; edge SKUs require rugged operation (-40°C to 85°C) with dynamic temperature support.
motivation: 5G/6G edge computing and network functions demand flexible SoC architectures that can scale across both high-performance (data-center style) and rugged-edge deployment scenarios, with integrated security and multi-protocol networking.
method: Granite Rapids-D is Intel's Xeon 6 processor in two specialized versions. One prioritizes computational performance—both sequential and parallel—using PCIe5 connections and low-latency memory for cloud data centers and vRAN (virtualized radio access networks). The other is built rugged: it operates from -40°C to 85°C with dynamic temperature management for harsh field conditions. Both include a secure processing area for confidential data (TEE—a protected zone where sensitive information can be processed securely) and support for ethernet and accelerators.
key_novelty: One processor family with two versions: one optimized for high-performance cloud work and one built to withstand extreme field temperatures.
contributions: Compute-optimized Xeon 6 SKU for vRAN, edge compute, and networking acceleration
Edge-optimized SKU with full rugged-temperature operation (-40°C to 85°C Tcase)
Integrated confidential AI security for edge deployment
PCIe5 and high-bandwidth memory for low-latency vRAN processing
limitations: Abstract provides market positioning but lacks specific performance metrics (core count, clock speed, power envelope, memory bandwidth), throughput benchmarks, or security TEE latency data.
primary_theme: Flexible dual-SKU SoC for edge compute and vRAN
